column1: # Accepted staleness in the config registry — the BACKLOG, with a reason per row.
# columns: the registry entry, the `path::symbol` its justification rests on, and
# why that row is accepted for now. The reason column may not be empty.
# THIS FILE IS A RATCHET, NOT A SUPPRESSION LIST. The gate fails on a stale row
# that is NOT here (a measurement newly gone stale) AND on a row here that is no
# longer stale (a line that has stopped describing anything). It can fail in both
# directions, which is what stops it becoming a checker that cannot fail.
# The right edit is to DELETE a line, having re-taken the measurement and moved
# the entry's `measured_on`. Adding a line is an admission and needs an argument.
# WHY IT EXISTS (ADR-2085, 2026-09-15). The gate reported 11 stale rows. Two were
# false positives of its own occurrence filter, one was flagged for its comments
# rather than its subject, and teaching it to notice a REWRITTEN FUNCTION BODY —
# which `git log -G<symbol>` structurally cannot see, because a body does not
# repeat its own name — took the true count to 24 across 14 entries. Clearing 24
# means fourteen corpus measurements. The two ways to go green without them are
# both forbidden by the gate's own rule: move the dates (the rubber stamp this
# check exists to prevent) or delete the `rests_on` entries (the same thing with
# extra steps). So the backlog is written down instead.
#   TRIAGED  — the diff was read line by line; the finding is stated.
#   DETECTED — found by the definition-drift signal on the day it was added and
#              NOT yet triaged. These are honest unknowns, not clean bills.
